text: The warehouse is built and waiting. Now we build the first third of the nightly SSIS package: Extract — pulling all fourteen stores' files into staging, with the failure handling we planned back in video seven actually wired in.

Before touching a single file, the package opens a load_batch row and checks the actual file count against the expected fourteen. If one's missing, it doesn't block the other thirteen — it logs exactly which store, alerts a human, and keeps going.

A ForEach loop walks every file that did arrive. Inside, every column from the flat file source gets typed as plain string, no exceptions — real type conversion happens deliberately later, in transform, not here.

The one configuration choice that matters most: the flat file source's error output gets explicitly redirected to the load_errors table, instead of left on its default behavior, which fails the whole component. That single switch turns one bad row crashing the night into one bad row getting logged, with everything else still loading.
Every row, good or bad, gets tagged with tonight's load_id before it lands — that's what makes any of this traceable later.
The stage logs its own completion to etl_run_log before moving on — the record a future diagnosis will depend on. Transform is next: turning these raw strings into real, trustworthy numbers.
